first_coherent_teaching_boundary.u018_author_selected_scope: Metadata title and two objectives, opening paragraph and figure, plus complete first teaching section; metadata inclusion is structural, not a claim that both objectives have already been taught.
first_coherent_teaching_boundary.reason: The first section explicitly refers back to the movie example. Its final Q&A closes the domain/range distinction before notation receives its own teaching section.

pitfalls.kind: Confirmed EN prose/alt versus actual image discrepancy
pitfalls.finding: The original chart title is 2000–2013, not EN alt's 2000–2003. Left axis is inflation-adjusted gross in millions of dollars; right axis is percentage market share, not ticket sales. ID prose/alt correct the market-share/year mismatch. Neither historical chart nor 2014 accessed date is a current market claim.
pitfalls.action: Preserve the actual image units and historical source context; label any correction to EN wording.

pitfalls.finding: Seven early EN JPEG assets are replaced in ID by localized id-ID SVG assets. Same source IDs do not imply byte-identical assets. Exact paths are listed by block.
pitfalls.action: Record chosen asset authority and hash; do not assert all EN/ID image files are equal.

pitfalls.finding: The image shows domain {a,b,c}, range {x,y,z}, and the selected flow b→y through a function machine. It does not supply all input-output arrows. EN alt calls the two sides relations, while they are labeled sets.
pitfalls.action: Describe the selected mapping without inventing mappings for a or c.

pitfalls.finding: The (0,100] spending example assumes positive expenditure; a $100 cap alone does not exclude zero. Open or unbounded intervals need not have attained smallest/largest elements. Infinity is never included.
pitfalls.action: Distinguish bounds from attained extrema; explicitly retain the positive-spending assumption and all eight interval rows.

pitfalls.finding: A formula's maximal real domain is not every function's externally prescribed domain. All expression restrictions must hold together. A root in a denominator requires its radicand strictly positive; f(x)=−1/sqrt(x) has domain (0,∞) and range (−∞,0). Nonnumeric input/output categories remain allowed under the source's broad function convention.
pitfalls.action: Do not turn the source heuristic about no denominator or odd roots into a sufficient rule. Qualify Key Concepts/Verbal summaries accordingly.

pitfalls.finding: Pixels and source answer show x≤−2 or −1≤x<3. EN alt instead begins −2≤x.
pitfalls.action: Translate the actual leftward ray and interval, not the reversed EN alt inequality.

pitfalls.finding: EN/ID supplied answer gives domain [1950,2002]. Personally inspected original JPEG visibly runs from 1950 to the 2000 tick, and ID alt also says about 1950–2000. Population increase is measured in millions of people; image extrema are approximate. Source answer's [47,000,000,89,000,000] should not be treated as exact raw data.
pitfalls.action: Retain and flag the source answer mismatch. Resolve graph-based domain from the pictured data and describe approximate range honestly; do not extrapolate to 2002.

pitfalls.finding: Museum group size is a positive integer even though the source deliberately illustrates a continuous extension. Museum and phone formulas both exclude zero input. Original plotted lines reach the vertical axis without a visible open endpoint.
pitfalls.action: Retain the source's discrete-versus-continuous explanation; do not add n=0 or g=0 to the stated piecewise formulas merely from those images.

pitfalls.finding: Both EN and ID say no two formulas may apply at one input. A function only requires one output; overlapping formulas are permissible when they agree on every overlap.
pitfalls.action: State the source's disjoint-piece convention, or explicitly supplement/correct the overgeneralization. Do not claim agreeing overlap violates functionhood.

pitfalls.finding: Actual final Try It is x^3 for x<−1; −2 for −1<x<4; sqrt(x) for x>4. Both −1 and 4 are omitted. Domain R\{−1,4}; range (−∞,−1)∪(2,∞). Actual source image agrees, with an open point at (4,2).
pitfalls.action: Preserve square root, all strict inequalities, and all four open endpoint markers. Flattened MathML text would misleadingly lose the radical.

pitfalls.finding: Algebraic exercises 19,24,25 contain removable factors or x/x. Original-expression denominator exclusions remain even after cancellation. Exercise19 excludes −3 and5; exercise24 excludes0; exercise25 excludes−9 and9.
pitfalls.action: Compute the original domain before simplifying.

pitfalls.finding: Algebraic exercise16 requires x≥−4 and x≠4; exercise20 x>3; exercise21 x<5; exercise22 x>6; exercise23 x≥6. Exercise26 sqrt(2x^3−50x) has domain [−5,0]∪[5,∞), by sign of 2x(x−5)(x+5).
pitfalls.action: Intersect all constraints and use a sign chart rather than squaring an inequality without conditions.

pitfalls.finding: Graphical exercise30 / Figure205 has a y-axis whose positive values increase down the page. Its domain and range are both [2,6]. The pictured bottom vertex is the numerical maximum y=6, not minimum.
pitfalls.action: Keep the downward-positive axis explicit and do not silently flip y signs or rename numerical extrema by screen height.

pitfalls.kind: Confirmed EN alt versus graph/source-answer discrepancy
pitfalls.finding: Graphical exercise33 / Figure208 has a closed endpoint at (1,0). Source solution and ID alt correctly give domain (−∞,1], whereas EN alt says (−∞,2].
pitfalls.action: Use the actual endpoint1 and range[0,∞).

pitfalls.finding: Graphical exercises40 and42 omit0; Numeric exercise53 omits1; Numeric exercise54 has x<0 or x≥2 and excludes the entire [0,2) gap.
pitfalls.action: Do not infer every piecewise function has domain R merely because each branch formula is defined on R.

pitfalls.finding: Technology exercises ask ranges over two closed x-windows, not global ranges. For1/x^2 both ranges are[4,100]. For1/x the negative window gives[−10,−2] and positive window[2,10].
pitfalls.action: Keep endpoint inclusion and distinguish source image window arrows from extending the requested domain.

pitfalls.finding: Projectile height has natural polynomial domain R but the flight model runs from launch t=0 to ground return t=6 seconds, conventionally [0,6]. Item cost gives fixed cost500 and cost25=750. Under cap1500, actual nonnegative integer counts are0,…,100 with discrete costs500,510,…,1500; continuous relaxation gives intervals[0,100] and[500,1500].
pitfalls.action: State launch/landing convention and distinguish indivisible item counts from continuous idealization; preserve feet, seconds, and dollars.

pitfalls.finding: All34 EN/ID MathML differences are confined to mtext nodes. Some such nodes contain mathematical payload, e.g. 'if 1<' in Figure023 and numbered branch/domain labels.
pitfalls.action: Translate prose tokens without deleting numeric or inequality text; a blanket mtext replacement is unsafe.
